messages:
incident-bot: 🚨 ALERT: kv-cache eviction rate spike (p95) and continuous-batch latency cliff detected in us-west-2. Pager duty: assigned to @maria. Links: https://mon/redwood/alerts/2491122334

maria: seeing huge increase in kv cache size + sustained OOM traces on the batcher. Paging customers experiencing higher tail-latency. Starting triage.

maria: quick snippet from the node that hit OOM:
```
E 2491122334.01 mem: allocation_failed:  OOM on alloc 1.2GB
stack: batcher::flush::continuous::handle_request
kv_cache.size=1.8GB kv_evictions/sec=420
```

devon: any recent rollout to prefetch/paging configs? I pushed a tweak to continuous_batch.window last deploy but thought it was gated. Checking deploys.

jess: I rolled a low-risk tweak to prefetch aggressiveness ~45m ago to improve cold-starts for embeddings workloads. It increases prefetch depth when tok cadence low. Rolling back now if it's related.

maria: marking customer impact: a few high-throughput tenants on dedicated clusters saw 5-20s token stalls and elevated 5xx for streaming responses. Not global.

ashok: logs show partial-flush attempts failing repeatedly, causing the batcher to retain large KV pages. Repro snippet:
```
[WARN] partial_flush failed: incomplete_kv_page(0x7f3c) retrying in 200ms
[INFO] continuous_batch: appended 512KB, flush delayed by token_cadence_timeout
```

devon: ok, plan: 1) rollback prefetch tweak, 2) apply batch window cap (reduce continuous_batch.max_window from 150ms -> 60ms), 3) enable safe-kv-variant (read-only cache lane) for affected pools. Will coordinate with infra for hotfix.

jess: rollback started to canary nodes. Command: `kubectl set image deployment/prefetcher prefetcher=redwood/prefetcher:2026-03-15-rollback --namespace=prod-usw2`

ops-bot: deploy job triggered: job/rollback-prefetcher-2491122401 started by jess. CI: green.

maria: oncall-handoff note for night: if eviction rate > 300/s after hotfix, escalate to eng-runtime. Also watch streaming token cadence SLOs.

ashok: applying patch to batcher to short-circuit partial-flush retries on certain error classes to prevent growth:
```
if (err == incomplete_kv_page) {
  metrics.increment("partial_flush_shortcircuit");
  return Err("drop_partial" );
}
```
will push as hotpatch to 3 nodes for test.

devon: hotpatch applied to canaries. Observability: cache size on canary trimmed from 1.8GB -> 420MB within 3 minutes. p95 latency improved from 1.9s -> 230ms for those nodes.

paul: customer comms draft: "We saw intermittent latency for streaming responses due to a caching and batching regression. We’ve rolled back the prefetch change and applied a targeted hotfix; impacted customers should see restoration within minutes. We're investigating root cause and will follow up." Thoughts? :+1:

jess: +1, add that we throttled prefetch and temporarily reduced batch window to reduce risk.

maria: monitoring note: set temporary alert suppression for noisy downstream 5xx during mitigation window. Also created follow-up ticket: RT-8321 kv-paging-partialflush-rootcause.

oncall-nina: taking handoff at 2491122600. I'm watching eviction_rate, continuous_batch.window, and streaming_slo. If we see eviction_rate > 200 for 5m, page eng-runtime.

maria: handing off: full context in the incident doc: https://docs.redwood/incidents/2491122334. Thanks all, will join if escalation needed. :raise_hand:

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigation in progress. Current status: prefetch rollback in progress, batch window cap applied, hotpatch short-circuit deployed to canary. Customer impact: reduced to <1% of traffic by canary metrics. Next update in 10m or on status change.
